result.topic_en: Gauss derives an expression for the differential of the lateral (geodesic) curvature of a curve on a surface in terms of the first fundamental form coefficients P, Q, R and the direction components t', θ', separating off the part integrable as an arctangent ψ.
result.transcription:
Math 29
Seitenkrümmung

Jst $df$ das Differential der Seitenkrümmung, welches dem Differential $du$ entspricht, so ist in den Zeichen der Entwicklung

$2(Pt't'+2Qt'\theta'+R\theta'\theta').\sqrt{(PR-QQ)}.df =$
$2(PR-QQ)(t'd\theta'-\theta'dt')$
$+t'^3(-QP'+2PQ'-PP'')du$
$+t't'\theta'(-RP'+2QQ'+2PR'-3QP'')du$
$+t'\theta'\theta'(3QR'-2RP''-2QQ''+PR'')du$
$+\theta'^3(RR'-2RQ''+QR'')du$

Wenn man bloss das erste Glied des zweiten Theils der Gleichung berücksichtigt ist das Integral
$f = \mathrm{Arc.tang}\frac{\theta'\sqrt{(PR-QQ)}}{Pt'+Q\theta'} + \mathrm{Const.} = \psi + \mathrm{Const.}$

Aus der vollständigen Differentiation von $\psi$ erhält man aber
$2(Pt't'+2Qt'\theta'+R\theta'\theta')\sqrt{(PR-QQ)}.d\psi =$
$2(PR-QQ)(t'd\theta'-\theta'dt')$
$+((2QQ-PR)t'\theta'+QR\theta'\theta')\frac{dP}{P}$
$-2(Qt'\theta'+R\theta'\theta').dQ$
$+(Pt'\theta'+Q\theta'\theta').dR$

| weil $\tang\psi = \frac{a\sqrt{b}}{c}$ gesetzt
| $2(cc+aab)d\psi = 2bc\,da + ac\,db - 2ab\,dc$

Dies substituirt erhalten wir
$2(Pt't'+2Qt'\theta'+R\theta'\theta').\sqrt{(PR-QQ)}.(df-d\psi) =$
$t'^3(-QP'+2PQ'-PP'')du$
$+t't'\theta'(-\frac{2QQ}{P}.P'+4QQ'+PR'-3QP'')du$
$+t'\theta'\theta'(-\frac{QR}{P}.P'+2RQ'-\frac{PR+2QQ}{P}.P''+2QR')du$
$+\theta'^3(RR'[?]-\frac{QR}{P}P'')du$

$=(Pt't'+2Qt'u'+Ru'u')[(-\frac{QP'}{P}+2Q'-P'')t'du+(R'-\frac{QP''}{P})\theta'du]$
